question: What is the primary purpose of sterilization in clinical practice?

options.A: Prevention of rusting on metal tools
options.B: Removal of visible dirt and dust only
options.C: Complete elimination of all microbial life
options.D: Reduction of bacteria to safe levels

explanation: Sterilization destroys every form of microbial life, including resistant spores, unlike disinfection which only reduces pathogen numbers. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h1)

question: Why must instruments be thoroughly washed before entering a sterilizer?

options.A: Soap activates the chemical process inside the machine
options.B: Organic debris protects germs from the sterilizing agent
options.C: Washing prevents the autoclave chamber from rusting
options.D: Dry blood makes metal instruments too heavy to lift

explanation: Residual blood and tissue can shield microorganisms from heat or steam, causing sterilization failure. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h1)

question: What is the standard temperature used for steam sterilization in a basic autoclave?
explanation: The standard temperature of 121°C combined with steam pressure effectively kills bacterial spores. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h2)

question: A nurse notices the autoclave chamber is tightly packed to the top. What is the expected outcome?

options.B: Steam will fail to reach all surfaces
options.C: Items will dry out much faster than usual
options.D: The cycle time will automatically shorten

explanation: Overcrowding prevents steam penetration, leaving inner items unsterilized despite running the machine. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h2)

question: Which items are best suited for dry heat sterilization in an oven?

options.C: Cloth surgical gowns and linen packs

explanation: Dry heat does not rust sharp edges or damage dry glassware, making it appropriate for these specific items. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h3)

question: Why is boiling instruments in water for twenty minutes considered disinfection rather than true sterilization?

options.A: Water temperature drops too quickly during the process
options.B: Boiling introduces minerals that coat the metal
options.C: It fails to reliably destroy bacterial endospores
options.D: Microbes develop immediate resistance to hot water

explanation: While boiling kills most vegetative bacteria and viruses, tough endospores survive 100°C temperatures. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h3)

question: Which monitoring method provides the most reliable proof that sterilization was successful?

options.A: Chemical indicator tape on instrument packs
options.B: Visual inspection of dry metal surfaces

explanation: Biological indicators directly test whether the cycle kills highly resistant test spores, confirming true sterility. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h4)

question: What does a color change on a chemical indicator strip signify?

options.A: Every single microbe inside the pack is dead
options.B: The instrument has been stored long enough
options.C: The pack was exposed to sterilizing conditions
options.D: The machine is completely free of mechanical faults

explanation: Chemical indicators show that heat or steam reached the exterior pack, but they do not guarantee total spore destruction. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h4)

question: What causes strike-through contamination when removing items from an autoclave?

options.A: Opening the door while pressure is zero
options.B: Using chemical indicator tape on paper
options.C: Placing hot packs on a cold wet surface
options.D: Storing dry packs in a wooden cabinet

explanation: Condensation forms when hot packs touch cold surfaces, pulling moisture and airborne microbes through the wrapper. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h5)

question: How is the shelf life of a sterile wrapped instrument pack determined today?

options.A: By a strict limit of exactly seven days from processing
options.B: By the total number of times the autoclave was opened
options.C: By environmental events that could compromise the wrapper
options.D: By the expiry date printed on the chemical tape

explanation: Sterility is event-related; a package stays sterile until the wrapper is damaged, wet, or opened. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h5)
